mathematical_reason: CSUSM Chapter 9 Definitions 1–3 explicitly define the real-number model as equivalence classes of rational Cauchy sequences and define arithmetic classwise. This construction does not identify sequences with their rational limits; representatives may not converge in Q. Independence of representatives, field laws, an order and the least-upper-bound property are mathematical proof obligations and must not be regarded as part of the bare quotient definition.

CSUSM Chapter 9 Section 5 and the rational-Cauchy model distinguish strict positivity from mere eventual positivity of sequence terms. The null sequence 1/n has every term positive yet represents zero, so only an eventual uniform bound by a positive rational number defines a positive class. Representative independence follows by an epsilon comparison and is necessary before defining the ordered-field relation.
